passages.text: Brothers, I could not address you as spiritual, but as worldly—as infants in Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the believers in Corinth.
Paul calls them brothers.
Paul could not speak to them as spiritual people.
Paul had to speak to them as worldly people.
Paul saw them as infants in Christ.
passages.original: Κἀγώ ἀδελφοί οὐκ ἠδυνήθην λαλῆσαι ὑμῖν ὡς πνευματικοῖς ἀλλ’ ὡς σαρκίνοις ὡς νηπίοις ἐν Χριστῷ

passages.text: I gave you milk, not solid food, for you were not yet ready for solid food. In fact, you are still not ready, for you are still worldly. For since there is jealousy and dissension among you, are you not worldly? Are you not walking in the way of man?
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the Corinthian Christians.
Paul says, "I gave you milk."
I did not give you solid food.
You were not ready for solid food.
Even now, you are still not ready.
You are still worldly.
There is jealousy among you.
There is dissension among you.
This shows you are worldly.
You are living like ordinary people.
passages.original: γάλα ὑμᾶς ἐπότισα οὐ βρῶμα οὔπω γὰρ ἐδύνασθε Ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ ἔτι νῦν δύνασθε ἔτι γὰρ σαρκικοί ἐστε ὅπου γὰρ ἐν ὑμῖν ζῆλος καὶ ἔρις οὐχὶ σαρκικοί ἐστε καὶ κατὰ ἄνθρωπον περιπατεῖτε

passages.text: For when one of you says, “I follow Paul,” and another, “I follow Apollos,” are you not mere men?
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the Corinthian church.
He calls them brothers.
He says they are acting in a worldly way.
He says they are like infants in Christ.
He gives an example.
One person says, "I follow Paul."
Another person says, "I follow Apollos."
Paul asks a question.
He says, "Are you not acting like mere men?"
He means they are behaving in a human way, not a spiritual way.
They show division and jealousy.
This shows they are still worldly.
passages.original: ὅταν γὰρ λέγῃ τις Ἐγὼ μέν εἰμι Παύλου ἕτερος δέ Ἐγὼ Ἀπολλῶ οὐκ ἄνθρωποί ἐστε

passages.text: What then is Apollos? And what is Paul? They are servants through whom you believed, as the Lord has assigned to each his role.
passages.sermon:
Apollos is a servant.
Paul is a servant.
God gave each servant a role.
You believed through these servants.
The Lord assigned a role to each one.
passages.original: Τί οὖν ἐστιν Ἀπολλῶς τί δέ ἐστιν Παῦλος διάκονοι δι’ ὧν ἐπιστεύσατε καὶ ἑκάστῳ ὡς ὁ Κύριος ἔδωκεν

passages.text: I planted the seed and Apollos watered it, but God made it grow.
passages.sermon:
Paul is a servant of Jesus Christ.
Paul planted the seed of faith.
Apollos is also a servant of Jesus Christ.
Apollos watered the seed of faith.
God made the seed grow.
passages.original: ἐγὼ ἐφύτευσα Ἀπολλῶς ἐπότισεν ἀλλὰ ὁ Θεὸς ηὔξανεν

passages.text: So neither he who plants nor he who waters is anything, but only God, who makes things grow.
passages.sermon:
God makes things grow.
The person who plants is not important.
The person who waters is not important.
Only God is important.
God gives the growth.
passages.original: ὥστε οὔτε ὁ φυτεύων ἐστίν τι οὔτε ὁ ποτίζων ἀλλ’ ὁ αὐξάνων Θεός

passages.text: He who plants and he who waters are one in purpose, and each will be rewarded according to his own labor.
passages.sermon: The person who plants and the person who waters work together for the same purpose.\r\nEach person will receive a reward.\r\nGod will give each person a reward for his own work.
passages.original: ὁ φυτεύων δὲ καὶ ὁ ποτίζων ἕν εἰσιν ἕκαστος δὲ τὸν ἴδιον μισθὸν λήμψεται κατὰ τὸν ἴδιον κόπον

passages.text: For we are God’s fellow workers; you are God’s field, God’s building.
passages.sermon:
We work together with God.
We are God’s fellow workers.
You belong to God.
You are like a field that God owns.
You are like a building that God owns.
passages.original: Θεοῦ γάρ ἐσμεν συνεργοί Θεοῦ γεώργιον Θεοῦ οἰκοδομή ἐστε

passages.text: By the grace God has given me, I laid a foundation as an expert builder, and someone else is building on it. But each one must be careful how he builds.
passages.sermon:
God gave me grace.
I used this grace.
I laid a foundation.
I worked as an expert builder.
Someone else is building on this foundation.
Each person must be careful how he builds.
passages.original: Κατὰ τὴν χάριν τοῦ Θεοῦ τὴν δοθεῖσάν μοι ὡς σοφὸς ἀρχιτέκτων θεμέλιον ἔθηκα ἄλλος δὲ ἐποικοδομεῖ ἕκαστος δὲ βλεπέτω πῶς ἐποικοδομεῖ

passages.text: For no one can lay a foundation other than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon:
Jesus Christ is the foundation.
God already laid this foundation.
No one can lay any other foundation.
passages.original: θεμέλιον γὰρ ἄλλον οὐδεὶς δύναται θεῖναι παρὰ τὸν κείμενον ὅς ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός

passages.text: If anyone builds on this foundation using gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, or straw, his workmanship will be evident, because the Day will bring it to light. It will be revealed with fire, and the fire will prove the quality of each man’s work.
passages.sermon:
Anyone can build on this foundation.
He may use gold.
He may use silver.
He may use precious stones.
He may use wood.
He may use hay.
He may use straw.
Each person’s work will become clear.
The Day will show it.
Fire will reveal it.
The fire will test the quality of each person’s work.
passages.original: Εἰ δέ τις ἐποικοδομεῖ ἐπὶ τὸν θεμέλιον χρυσόν ἄργυρον λίθους τιμίους ξύλα χόρτον καλάμην ἑκάστου τὸ ἔργον φανερὸν γενήσεται ἡ γὰρ ἡμέρα δηλώσει ὅτι ἐν πυρὶ ἀποκαλύπτεται καὶ ἑκάστου τὸ ἔργον ὁποῖόν ἐστιν τὸ πῦρ αὐτὸ δοκιμάσει

passages.text: If what he has built survives, he will receive a reward.
passages.sermon:
A person builds on the foundation of Jesus Christ.
He does work on this foundation.
If his work remains,
he will receive a reward.
passages.original: εἴ τινος τὸ ἔργον μενεῖ ὃ ἐποικοδόμησεν μισθὸν λήμψεται

passages.text: If it is burned up, he will suffer loss. He himself will be saved, but only as if through the flames.
passages.sermon: If a person's work is burned up, he will lose his reward.\r\nHe will still be saved.\r\nHe will be saved as if escaping through fire.
passages.original: εἴ τινος τὸ ἔργον κατακαήσεται ζημιωθήσεται αὐτὸς δὲ σωθήσεται οὕτως δὲ ὡς διὰ πυρός

passages.text: Do you not know that you yourselves are God’s temple, and that God’s Spirit dwells in you?
passages.sermon: You are God’s temple.\r\nGod’s Spirit lives in you.
passages.original: Οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ναὸς Θεοῦ ἐστε καὶ τὸ Πνεῦμα τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν ὑμῖν οἰκεῖ

passages.text: If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy him; for God’s temple is holy, and you are that temple.
passages.sermon:
You are God’s temple.
God’s Spirit lives in you.
God’s temple is holy.
You are that temple.
If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy that person.
passages.original: εἴ τις τὸν ναὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ φθείρει φθερεῖ τοῦτον ὁ Θεός ὁ γὰρ ναὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ἅγιός ἐστιν οἵτινές ἐστε ὑμεῖς

passages.text: Let no one deceive himself. If any of you thinks he is wise in this age, he should become a fool, so that he may become wise.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the church in Corinth.
Paul warns the believers.
No one should deceive himself.
If anyone among you thinks he is wise in this age, he must become a fool.
He must do this so that he may become truly wise.
passages.original: Μηδεὶς ἑαυτὸν ἐξαπατάτω εἴ τις δοκεῖ σοφὸς εἶναι ἐν ὑμῖν ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τούτῳ μωρὸς γενέσθω ἵνα γένηται σοφός

passages.text: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness in God’s sight. As it is written: “He catches the wise in their craftiness.”
passages.sermon:
God sees everything.
God knows what is wise and what is foolish.
The wisdom of this world is foolishness to God.
Scripture says, “God catches the wise in their craftiness.”
God exposes those who think they are wise.
God does not value the clever plans of worldly people.
passages.original: ἡ γὰρ σοφία τοῦ κόσμου τούτου μωρία παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ ἐστιν γέγραπται γάρ Ὁ δρασσόμενος τοὺς σοφοὺς ἐν τῇ πανουργίᾳ αὐτῶν

passages.text: And again, “The Lord knows that the thoughts of the wise are futile.”
passages.sermon: The Lord knows everything.\r\nThe Lord knows the thoughts of wise people.\r\nThe Lord sees that these thoughts are useless.
passages.original: καὶ πάλιν Κύριος γινώσκει τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς τῶν σοφῶν ὅτι εἰσὶν μάταιοι

passages.text: Therefore, stop boasting in men. All things are yours, whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or the world or life or death or the present or the future. All of them belong to you, and you belong to Christ, and Christ belongs to God.
passages.sermon:
Do not boast about people.
God gives you all things.
Paul belongs to you.
Apollos belongs to you.
Cephas belongs to you.
The world belongs to you.
Life belongs to you.
Death belongs to you.
The present belongs to you.
The future belongs to you.
All these things belong to you.
You belong to Christ.
Christ belongs to God.
passages.original: Ὥστε μηδεὶς καυχάσθω ἐν ἀνθρώποις πάντα γὰρ ὑμῶν ἐστιν εἴτε Παῦλος εἴτε Ἀπολλῶς εἴτε Κηφᾶς εἴτε κόσμος εἴτε ζωὴ εἴτε θάνατος εἴτε ἐνεστῶτα εἴτε μέλλοντα πάντα ὑμῶν ὑμεῖς δὲ Χριστοῦ Χριστὸς δὲ Θεοῦ
